terms.meaning: a widely used open-source database program
a tool that runs programs in isolated packages called containers
the one setting that holds the database address, user and password
the numbered door on a computer that a program listens on

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Settings and early exit
sections.what: Loads the environment files, then reads the connection address and refuses to start without one.
sections.why: The address is the single source for the host and port.
sections.watch_out: The local settings file is read first and wins over the general one.

sections.name: url
sections.title: Split the address
sections.what: Splits the address into host, port, user, password, database name and the data folder path.
sections.why: The built-in database needs these as separate values.
sections.watch_out: The data folder path is based on the current folder, so running from another folder creates a second database.

sections.name: reachable, waitFor
sections.title: Check and wait for the port
sections.what: Checks whether something accepts connections on the port, and repeats the check until it does or time runs out.
sections.why: Waiting avoids starting a second copy.
sections.watch_out: The check only sees an open port, not a database that actually works.

sections.name: foreground
sections.title: Run the built-in database in the foreground
sections.what: Starts the built-in database in this process, creates the database if missing, and keeps it running until stopped.
sections.why: The background mode starts this same mode in a separate process.
sections.watch_out: A hard kill can skip the clean shutdown.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Choose how to start
sections.what: Skips if the database is already reachable, refuses non-local hosts, uses Docker compose when Docker is available, and otherwise starts a detached background copy of itself and waits.
sections.why: The order matches the file header.
sections.watch_out: The background copy is started from the script's own file path, which can break on some systems.

summary: Starts the local PostgreSQL database the app needs, using Docker if it is available or a built-in copy if not.
purpose: Lets the owner start a working local database with one command.
why: The file header states the order: already running, then Docker, then the built-in copy.
how: Reads the connection address, checks whether the port answers, refuses non-local hosts, uses Docker compose if Docker responds, otherwise starts a background process running an embedded Postgres in a data folder, and waits up to a minute.
inputs: DATABASE_URL from the environment files, and an optional foreground flag.
outputs: A running database, a log file in .data, and a status message.
risks: Any program answering on the port counts as the database. The database password is passed to the embedded server.
debug: Check .data/postgres.log. Run with the foreground flag to see errors directly.
